title: Leave the hunt to the learner
statement: In independent practice, leave the search to the learner: don't pre-mark candidates, name where to look, or say how many to find in an open hunt.
example: One audit found an independent hunt that pre-highlighted 8 segments and told the child to tap the three clues.
detail: A curriculum adherence audit (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/REPORT.md`, 2026-09-24) compared served independent tasks with designs that ask for an open hunt in which nothing is pre-highlighted. In three lessons the served hunts pre-highlighted their candidates and said how many to find, one with 8 highlighted segments and "Tap the three clues", and a multiple-choice zoom step named the evidence region first, which the audit says undoes the open hunt. The lesson-components list describes independent practice as clicking the evidence in the passage rather than choosing from options (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/inputs/procedures/Example_Lesson_Components.txt`).
against: One governing design itself shows a count, a tracker reading "{n} of 2 found", and whether a hunt can run with nothing pre-highlighted was left to a ruling on the engine (the same report, lines 46 and 48). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/round-5/open-hunt/CAUSE-PROPOSAL-IMPLEMENTATION.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/extras/alpharead-lesson-design-witw-part-1.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/pp2-v3-design.txt`).
